A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Holmes-VAU and HIVAU-70k. All 21 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original anomaly-detection and reasoning results, ablations and qualitative comparisons in Tables 1–4 and the main-text and appendix figures.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including detection scores, reasoning evaluations, ablations and appendix qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: Holmes-VAU retains the same anomaly scorer, density-aware temporal sampler, InternVL2-based architecture and two-stage training procedure. The data-annotation pipeline and appendix architecture details are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same HIVAU-70k coverage derived from UCF-Crime and XD-Violence, with clip-, event- and video-level tasks. Video-MME remains the general-capability evaluation; no new domain or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the detection and reasoning comparisons and sampling ablations. Table 1 adds publication venues and years to existing methods, rather than adding baselines.

E3.justification: The reported training settings, metrics, model configurations and sampling protocols remain unchanged. The new per-granularity test counts document the existing evaluation; neither version establishes a changed test set or rerun.

E4.justification: The hierarchical-data ablation, sampling-method and frame-count comparisons, LoRA analysis, anomaly-score visualizations and qualitative case studies are retained. Figure 5 rearranges existing examples without adding an analysis.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting remains unchanged. No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 1–4 and the plotted and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Holmes-VAU retains 87.68% AP on XD-Violence and 88.96% AUC on UCF-Crime. Appendix Figures G–J are pixel-identical.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), including the cumulative anomaly-score sampling definition and anomaly-scorer losses, retain the same mathematics. No formal assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: hierarchical anomaly annotations, the anomaly-focused sampler, and improved anomaly understanding and efficiency. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The limitations concerning streaming deployment, domain generalization and additional modalities already appear on v1 page 9. They move to Appendix E in v2 with equivalent meaning. Interpretations of the experimental findings are retained.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly specifies 2,200/732/398 clip/event/video test samples, and Figure 5 adds video identifiers. These improve documentation without establishing changed experiments. However, the counts total 3,330 while the retained text states 3,300.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds three references covering skeleton-based action recognition, temporal action-proposal generation and multimodal action recognition. The positioning argument remains unchanged. UR-DMU's updated publication information refers to the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: The existing limitations paragraph moves from the post-conclusion text to Appendix E. v2 also expands the funding acknowledgement and makes limited punctuation and wording edits; the broader narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 5 reorganizes the same response boxes and adds video-identifier labels. Table 1 adds venue/year annotations and adjusts its formatting. Other displays retain their content, with limited layout and pagination shifts.

improvement.justification: Figure 5's video identifiers and the newly documented test-set composition modestly improve traceability and understanding of the evidence. The gains are limited: methods, results and substantive limitations are unchanged, and the added sample breakdown totals 3,330 despite the retained 3,300 total.
